solution: Using the mirror formula \(\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}\): side AD lies at object distance \(u=2f\), giving \(v=2f\), so its transverse magnification \(m_A=-\frac{v}{u}=-1\) and \(A'D'\) equals \(AD\) in height. Side BC lies at \(u=3f\): \(\frac{1}{v}=\frac{1}{f}-\frac{1}{3f}=\frac{2}{3f}\), so \(v=\frac{3f}{2}\) and \(m_B=-\frac{v}{u}=-\frac{1}{2}\); thus \(B'C'\) is half of \(BC\). Since \(AD=BC\) (opposite sides of the rectangle), the ratio \(\frac{B'C'}{A'D'}=\frac{1}{2}\). Matches option C.

For a concave mirror, an object at infinity forms its image at the focus \(F\), while an object at the centre of curvature \(C\) forms its image at \(C\). As the object moves from far beyond \(C\) towards the mirror (towards \(C\)), the real image therefore travels from \(F\) outwards towards \(C\). Hence the image accelerates towards the centre of curvature. Matches option A.
